items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Nancy? I think she’s got an integrated small group.

ctx.x: Be integrated more? Yeah, it should be. Well you know they have it in the smaller groups they don’t have the big bands really to mix it more, with more, because we don’t have big bands. But that’s one thing that they never paid much attention to, you know? Of course © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Benny would do what he wanted to do, and so did Jimmy, Jimmy Dorsey. He had a girl named, black girl named June Richmond and boy she could sing, boy. And he brought her from California all through Texas and everywhere with him. So you’ve got to give him credit for that. This was Jimmy, not Tommy, Jimmy, his brother, you know? And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band, and Sy Oliver was writing all these arrangements. So there was more integration, more. Of course we had more musicians and as I…
A couple of last questions I would like to ask you. Was the Basie band the best big band there ever was?
